newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.10 lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.10 lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to 0.10 cent lower Thursday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, trading sources said.
They expect prices to ease from 15-week highs reached Wednesday, mostly on a disappointing export and sales report for the week ended June 19.
USDA put new sales at 50,400 480-lb bales for upland cotton in the new crop, and at 15,100 bales for the current crop. Shipments of upland cotton reached 115,400 bales for the current season.

"This was just a so-so report," Carl Anderson, a cotton marketing specialist with Texas A & M University, said. "We've fallen a bit below our weekly needs to reach the USDA target 7.1 million bales (exports) for this year."

Traders agreed, and said the market is likely to consolidate recent gains during today's session. A move higher would signal expectations for a sharp cut in the USDA's planted area estimate on Monday.
"Otherwise, we are up against technical resistance," Anderson said.
Additionally, warmer temperatures have improved crop development in the Delta and Southeast, and in Texas.
Wednesday, benchmark December rose to a 15-week high on brisk speculative buying before closing at 77.44 cents per lb, up 0.51 cent. The rest of the board finished 0.45 to 0.65 cent firmer.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 23,000 lots.
NYCE said 97 notices were issued today, bringing the total number of notices to date, to 551.
